title: The writer always runs the tests it adds
description: Fixes F848 (quality-gates-internal PLAN.md), a recurrence of the class P157.12 closed for one shape. Blocks the stage-2 re-measurement.
desiredOutcome: Every writer brief of a task that declares tests.add files lists a command that runs each of them, whatever the gate's slow steps are spelled as, or says why none could be derived

tasks.title: Every tests.add suite the task declares is run by a command the writer brief lists: a slow step that names none of them is extended to them when its runner takes suite paths, and otherwise the brief names each suite it could not give a command for and why
tasks.description: F848. At 8407a02d compose_writer_prompt (plugins/audit/scripts/status/audit-lookup.py ~1082-1150) moves a slow gate step to `Do not run ... left to the phase gate` and calls own_suite_command (~1049) to keep the task's own suites runnable; own_suite_command returns None unless the step's command already names a tests.add file. A whole-tree step - this repo's `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py`, whose recorded mean is past FOREGROUND_BOUND_MS on the stage-2 bases v01, v02, v08 - names none, so the brief lists only validate/lint and the writer runs no test it wrote. P157.12 fixed the shape where the slow step names the suite; this is the same class in another shape, so the fix is the invariant, not a third shape: every _fr.tests_add_files(task) entry is covered by a listed command or by a stated reason. Deriving the command: a single simple command whose runner takes suite paths (the sweep runner does: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/a.py`) gets the uncovered suites appended in place of its own path arguments; decide how a runner is known to take suite paths from what _phases already knows about script runners and say how you decided, rather than a list of program names. The plain arm of the measurement is composed by this same function (both arms read it), so the wording stays task-only. measure-context's ceiling for the writer brief must hold.

tasks.title: A suite counts as run only by a command that really runs it: a filtered run is not a whole run, a suite goes only to a runner the plan hands that kind of suite, the phase gate's spellings are read, and the derived command keeps the step's own shell words
tasks.description: Phase code review of P158 (commit facd6f30, audit-lookup.py). MED1: _runs_whole_tree (~1168) reads any command whose non-flag words hold no path as a whole-tree run, so `python3 -m pytest -k smoke` counts as covering every suite and a tests.add suite gets no line; no case pins the branch (patching it to False leaves every ws case green). A whole run must be one the plan itself spells as the runner with no selection (no path and no selecting option), or count as not covering. MED2: suite_coverage (~1197) hands every unrun suite to the first known runner whatever the suite's kind; tie a runner to the kinds of suite the plan hands it (e.g. the suffix/extension of the paths it is spelled with) and give a reason line otherwise. MED3: _plan_commands (~1124) reads buildCommands values and tasks' tests.gate only; a phase testGate (and meta.fullGate when set) are plan spellings too, and the reason line must not claim no runner is known when the inherited gate spells one. MED4: _given_suites (~1165) shlex.quote()s every word after shlex split them, turning $ROOT/~ into literals; rebuild the derived command from the original command text (replace only the path words, keep the rest byte for byte), and give own_suite_command the same treatment so there is one way to derive a cut. LOW: --flag=suite words are lost (keep flags whole); non-suite tests.add files are handed to runners (filter with the suite-path reading); the compose_writer_prompt docstring still says the composition is the task alone's while it now reads the plan - state what it reads. One derivation shared by the cut and the extension, not two.

add: tests/test_audit_lookup.py: a fast listed 'python3 -m pytest -k smoke' (or --lf) is not a whole run, so a tests.add suite still gets a derived line or a reason line (red-first: no line today; _runs_whole_tree patched to False must turn a case red); a tests/ui.test.js suite is never handed to a runner the plan only ever hands .py suites, and gets a reason line instead; a task with no gate of its own inheriting a phase testGate that spells the sweep with a suite gets a derived command, not a false reason; a step spelled with $ROOT or ~ keeps that word unquoted in the derived command; a --only=<suite> flag word is kept as a flag, not replaced; a non-suite tests.add file (tests/fixtures/x.json) is not handed to a runner
